correctness.rationale: For the affine example, the separated penalty model is exact. On the radius interval centered at the reference point, the base penalty model has slope \(\gamma/2\), so its normalized Wolfe residual is exactly \(\gamma/2\); the feasibility inequality also holds with equality. Replacing \(\gamma\) by \(\tilde\gamma>\gamma\) changes the slope and exact residual to \(\tilde\gamma-\gamma/2\). The feasibility lower requirement is only \(\tilde\gamma/2\), so the Wolfe residual is the active minimum tolerance. Substituting \(\nu=\gamma/2\) into Proposition 4.3 gives exactly the same value. The package verifier checks these identities over exact rational test cases, and I independently reconstructed the algebra from Definition 3 and the proposition statement.

value.rationale: Proposition 4.3 is the mechanism that preserves certificates while the algorithm changes its penalty estimate. Showing its deterioration coefficient is genuinely unavoidable establishes that the parameter-update analysis cannot be uniformly improved by tightening that step alone. The one-dimensional affine example is simple because it is an extremal sharpness certificate, not because the constant is unmotivated.
